lead_development.title: Retailers are competing through transparency, digital reach and ownership convenience.
lead_development.what_happened: GM's CarBravo connects certified used inventory across participating dealers and reports that about 38% of initially used-car shoppers ultimately buy new. The FTC reached an agreement with Stream Auto Outlet over advertised prices that excluded required fees.
lead_development.why_it_matters: Used-car shoppers are increasingly valuable acquisition opportunities for new-vehicle retailers, but misleading pricing creates regulatory and reputational exposure. Convenience and transparent payments may matter as much as inventory breadth.

signals.title: Honda and Toyota Push Mainstream SUVs Toward Hybrid-Only Powertrains
signals.teaser: Honda announced that the redesigned 2028 CR-V will use a hybrid-only powertrain.

signals.title: New-Vehicle Affordability Is Tightening Despite Continued Incentives
signals.teaser: Kelley Blue Book reported a record $51,109 average transaction price in October, up 1.3% from September and 2.1% year over year.

signals.title: Automakers Are Rebuilding Around Regional Cost and Development Advantages
signals.teaser: Nissan plans to increase exports of China-developed vehicles from two models to five across 12 regional market clusters, citing lower costs, faster development and competitive technology.

downside.title: Affordability erosion could reduce retail conversion and increase payment-driven trade-down.
downside.teaser: Record transaction prices, a $776 average payment and rising lower-price sales indicate growing budget pressure.

upside.title: Expand hybrid inventory, sales training and payment-based merchandising.
upside.teaser: Honda and Toyota are moving high-volume SUVs toward hybrid-only lineups while hybrid penetration has increased.
